title: This Time-Lapse Video from the Psyche Spacecraft Shows Mars As You’ve Never Seen It Before
gist: A very short news item noting that NASA's Psyche spacecraft, en route to the metal-rich Psyche asteroid between Mars and Jupiter with arrival expected in 2029, returned new footage of Mars during its passing flyby. The written body carries only the flyby context — the promised time-lapse itself sits in an embedded video the text does not describe.

insights.claim: NASA's Psyche spacecraft is en route to the metal-rich Psyche asteroid located between Mars and Jupiter, with arrival expected in 2029.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A 2029 arrival date sets the clock on the first close study of a metal-rich body, the science event underpinning long-dated asteroid-resource narratives.
insights.quote: It comes from the NASA Psyche spacecraft, which is on its way to the metal-rich Psyche asteroid between Mars and Jupiter.
insights.locator: It comes from the NASA Psyche

insights.claim: The Mars leg of the Psyche mission doubles as a free rehearsal, letting NASA researchers exercise the probe's full instrument suite years before it reaches its actual target.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Piggybacking instrument checkout onto a trajectory that was needed anyway is the cost-discipline pattern that keeps deep-space mission budgets defensible.
insights.quote: The craft should reach Psyche in 2029, but Mars, of course, is along the way, giving NASA researchers an opportunity to test out the battery of instruments on board the probe
insights.locator: The craft should reach Psyche in 2029

insights.claim: Each successive photo and video returned from Mars incrementally sharpens understanding of the planet's surface, atmosphere, geological history, and composition.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Knowledge of Mars accrues from many cheap incidental passes rather than single flagship missions — a steady drip of data, not step-change events.
insights.quote: With every photo and video that comes back of Mars, we’re getting a clearer picture of the Red Planet: its surface, its atmosphere, its geological history, and its composition.
insights.locator: With every photo and video that comes back
